task: Clean junk and stale files from the iceberg_models repository
critical_rules: This repo contains 82 GB of irreplaceable downloaded data and a trained model. Re-downloading takes many hours (ERA5 goes through a queue).
NEVER delete anything under seaice_forecast/data/ unless it is explicitly named in delete_safe below.
NEVER delete anything under seaice_forecast/models/checkpoints/ - that is the trained model.
Run `git status` before deleting. If a file is modified-but-uncommitted, leave it and report it.
Print the total size of everything you plan to delete, and wait for confirmation before deleting more than 100 MB.
Move to a quarantine folder first (see procedure). Do not use `rm -rf` directly on anything except the always-safe patterns.

delete_safe.description: Remove these without asking. Zero risk.

delete_after_check.description: Almost certainly junk, but verify each is not referenced by any script before removing. Grep the repo for the filename first.

items.reason: Stray directory containing only path/to/commit_message.txt - an accidental `mkdir path/to/...`
Stray root-level src/index.js - unrelated to this Python project. NOTE: do NOT confuse with seaice_forecast/src/ which is the real package.
Two single-day CMEMS test downloads left in the project root. The real currents data lives in seaice_forecast/data/data/{YYYY}/.
Stale evaluation dump from an earlier reorganisation
Superseded test download. Confirm size before deleting; this is the largest single reclaim.

consolidate_docs.description: Many overlapping status/instruction markdown files accumulated. Do NOT delete them - move them to docs/archive/ and leave a single current README.

items.issue: Contains a hardcoded API key (sk-...) for an internal LLM endpoint, and is NOT gitignored. A `git add .` would commit the credential.
items.action: Add 'qwen_chat.py' and '.env' to .gitignore. Replace the literal key with os.environ['QWEN_API_KEY']. Do not delete the file.

never_touch: seaice_forecast/data/processed/**  (6.2 GB - the training set; deleting it means retraining is impossible)
seaice_forecast/data/data/{2008..2018}/**  (46 GB currents - hours to re-download)
seaice_forecast/data/data/raw/era5/**  (132 months, downloaded through a slow CDS queue)
seaice_forecast/data/data/raw/iceberg_positions/**  (1,543 tracks - needed for the drift model)
seaice_forecast/models/checkpoints/**  (the trained model and its backup)
procedure: 1. Run `git status` and record anything uncommitted.
4. For each item in delete_after_check: grep the repo for its basename. If referenced by any .py/.sh/.yaml, SKIP it and report. Otherwise MOVE it to quarantine.
5. Move the consolidate_docs candidates into docs/archive/.
6. Apply gitignore_additions (append, do not overwrite existing entries).
8. Print a summary table: file, action taken, size reclaimed.
9. Tell the user to verify the project still works, then delete the quarantine folder manually.
report_back: A table of what was deleted, what was archived, what was skipped and why, total space reclaimed, and confirmation that all 4 verification checks passed.
